perspective:
Gloria Bangura’s available information:

- She works with Donald at company events; she is an administrative assistant and he serves drinks as a bartender.
- Over several events, she directly observed that Donald seemed distracted and lacked enthusiasm while working.
- She approached him and asked if he was okay, specifically whether something was wrong with his job.
- Donald told her he wasn’t as into the job as he used to be and that it felt repetitive.
- After reflecting on their talk, she began to suspect his work dissatisfaction might point to deeper personal issues.
- She suggested he consider talking to a professional about what might be bothering him.
- Donald said he hadn’t considered that and wasn’t sure it would help.
- She then noticed a shift in Donald’s behavior toward her and believed he might resent her suggestion, feeling she had overstepped.
- She apologized to him, explaining she only wanted to help and didn’t mean to make assumptions.
- Donald told her he had been taken aback at first but knew she meant well, and that it was a lot to process.
- She felt the apology eased the tension and that they had cleared the air.
- She invited Donald to collaborate on an upcoming project because she wanted to strengthen their professional relationship and thought his input would be valuable.
- Donald accepted, saying he appreciated the offer and wanted to be more involved.
- During the project, she directly observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm.
- She concluded he was a valuable team member and publicly acknowledged his work in a team meeting.
- Donald thanked her, saying it meant a lot, that he was glad to contribute, and that being appreciated felt great.
